About the Role

East Avenue Medical Centre is seeking an experienced Registered Nurse to join our team as a driving force and advocate for preventative health in our local community. In this rewarding role, you will work closely alongside our General Practitioners and patients to identify, manage, and monitor chronic health conditions, ultimately improving long-term health outcomes and reducing preventable hospital admissions.
While clinical experience in Chronic Disease Management (CDM) is highly regarded, we place immense value on a friendly, proactive, supportive nature and a strong alignment with our collaborative practice culture.


Key Duties and Responsibilities

•	Prepare, implement, and review Care Plans and Team Care Arrangements (TCAs).
•	Conduct health assessments to assist in the early identification of chronic diseases.
•	Work collaboratively with GPs to promote preventative healthcare pathways throughout the practice.
•	Empower and coach patients to increase ownership over their health using behavior change principles.
•	Coordinate multi-disciplinary team care, enabling patients to access essential allied health services.
•	Manage administrative tasks and scheduling related to dedicated CDM and health assessment appointments.
•	Deliver home-based nursing care to eligible patients under the direct supervision and delegation of our GPs.
•	Actively work to increase the reach of preventative care plans to new and existing patients.


Requirements

•	Current registration as a Registered Nurse with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia (NMBA) / AHPRA.
•	Demonstrated experience in nursing (primary health care or general practice experience is an asset).
•	Strong communication skills with a compassionate, patient-centered approach.


Benefits

•	Professional development assistance and ongoing training support.
•	Generous employee discounts on services.
•	Performance and workplace incentives.



About the Company 

East Avenue Medical Centre has a proud and longstanding history, deeply rooted in the Glen Innes community. Established in 1969, the practice was the area's first general practice, marking the beginning of a long tradition of caring for the local community. Its vision was simple yet powerful: to provide accessible, compassionate, and high-quality healthcare to a growing community.

We also provide a comprehensive range of equipment and products, supporting the mining, oil & gas, and construction industries across Australia and internationally.

As a Project Administrator / Administrative Officer, you will provide administrative and project coordination support to project managers, engineers, supervisors, and operational teams. You will be responsible for maintaining project documentation, coordinating communications, monitoring project records, and ensuring administrative processes are completed accurately and efficiently to support the successful delivery of mining, industrial, and engineering projects.

•	Maintain confidentiality and ensure accurate record-keeping at all times.
•	Comply with workplace health and safety policies, company procedures, and quality management systems.

Skills and Experience
